newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Amnesty expires for Sri Lanka's illegal guns.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty expires for Sri Lanka's illegal guns.

text.p: An amnesty offered by Sri Lankan police for the surrender of unlicensed firearms expired on Saturday with the police vowing to pursue those who had failed to comply.
"Now we will launch a tough campaign to crack down on those who possess illegal firearms," a senior police officer, who wished to remain unidentified, told Reuters.
He said details of the outcome of the amnesty were not immediately available, but added that "a fairly substantial amount of (unlicensed) guns" were handed over to the police.
Police searches and voluntary handovers have netted more than 1,500 illegal weapons, deputy inspector general of the police crimes branch Mohammed Nizam told Reuters earlier this week.
The government this week announced it would enact new laws under the country's emergency regulations to crack down on users, mostly politicians and political activists, of illegal firearms.

The new laws, expected to be finalised in three weeks, provide for a minimum seven-year prison sentence and a maximum sentence of 20 years for possession of unlicensed guns and other firearms and the confiscation of the vehicle or house where illegal firearms are found.
The government also plans to make bail unavailable to those charged until the judicial process is completed.

Politicians and party activists in the Indian Ocean island carry guns, many of them unlicensed, to guard against attack by separatist Tamil rebels, who are fighting for independence in the island's north and east.

But their guns became a key public issue when a young legislator from Sri Lanka's ruling coalition government was gunned down last month. An opposition party member was among the suspects detained by police over the killing.
A local government election, to be held on March 21, also has been marred by violence with several incidents of shooting reported by politicians and their supporters.
